title: Averaging Multiple Results
text: settings, ’ll use ones given original t-SNE paper. ’ll run 10 embeddings. Note set ret_extra = TRUE ensure get back extra info let us work results lowest error (’ll need later). ’s code combine results smallvis_rep return median distance matrix: distance matrix-based refinement process can carried like : learning rate eta MMDS step found trial error. alternative approach ’ll just refine “best” result, first ’ll need extract best result output smallvis_rep. setting keep_all = TRUE ret_extra = TRUE, every result extra entry called best_rep, indicates results lowest error. looping result comparing last entry itercosts arrays, ’s obvious yet fiddly task smallvis_rep . resulting syntax extracting best result admittedly ugly: hand, can carry one t-SNE run best result result initial coordinates. original initialization, ’ll also consider even simpler case initialization Laplacian Eigenmaps (scaled PCA gives similar results, ’s little point using ). results regenerated alongside results , hopefully quite similar original initialization discussion. Although discussion indicated strong reason apply early exaggeration initializations, anyway just consistent random-initialized results.
code: # Generate 10 t-SNE embeddings iris_repn <- smallvis_rep(   n = 10,   keep_all = TRUE,   X = iris,   scale = FALSE,   perplexity = 40,   eta = 100,   exaggeration_factor = 4,   stop_lying_iter = 50,   ret_extra = TRUE ) combine_dy <- function(all_res, stat_fun = stats::median) {   res_dy <- NULL   nres <- length(all_res)   resi <- all_res[[1]]   if (class(resi) == "matrix") {     Y <- resi   } else {     Y <- resi$Y   }   nr <- nrow(Y)   dijs <- rep(0, nres)    res_dy <- matrix(0, nrow = nr, ncol = nr)   for (i in 1:(nr - 1)) {     for (j in (i + 1):nr) {       for (k in 1:nres) {         if (class(resi) == "matrix") {           Y <- all_res[[k]]         } else {           Y <- all_res[[k]]$Y         }         dijs[k] <- sqrt(sum((Y[i, ] - Y[j, ])^2))       }       res_dy[i, j] <- stat_fun(dijs)       res_dy[j, i] <- res_dy[i, j]     }   }    res_dy } iris_med <- combine_dy(iris_repn, stat_fun = stats::median) iris_med_mmds <- smallvis(   as.dist(iris_med),   method = "mmds",   scale = FALSE,   Y_init = "pca",   epoch = 5,   eta = 0.0001 ) iris_med_refine <- smallvis(   iris,   scale = FALSE,   perplexity = 40,   Y_init = iris_med_mmds,   eta = 100 ) iris_best <- iris_repn[[iris_repn[[1]]$best_rep]] iris_best_refine <- smallvis(   iris,   scale = FALSE,   perplexity = 40,   Y_init = iris_best$Y,   eta = 100,   exaggeration_factor = 4,   stop_lying_iter = 50 ) iris_le <- smallvis(   iris,   scale = FALSE,   perplexity = 40,   Y_init = "lap",   method = "tsne",   eta = 100,   exaggeration_factor = 4,   stop_lying_iter = 50 )

code: # generate force constants over a range of w pacmap_k <- function(a = 1, b = 10, n = 100, max_w = 0.99) {   w <- (1:n) / n   w <- w[w < max_w]   ka <- (2 * a * b * w * w) / ((1 + b * w)^2)   kr <- (-2 * w * w) / ((1 + w)^2)   list(attr = ka, rep = kr, w = w) }  umap_k <- function(a = 1.577, b = 0.895, n = 100, eps = 1e-3, max_w = 0.99) {   w <- (1:n) / n   w <- w[w < max_w]   d2 <- ((1 - w) / (a * w))^(1 / b)   d2b1 <- d2^(b - 1)    ka <- 2 * a * b * d2b1 * w   kr <- (-2 * b * w) / (eps + d2)   list(attr = ka, rep = kr, w = w) }  uk <- umap_k() tk <- umap_k(a = 1, b = 1) pk <- pacmap_k() pk3 <- pacmap_k(a = 3)  # Colors from: # inlmisc::GetColors(7, scheme = "bright")  lwd <- 2 plot(   uk$w,   uk$attr,   type = "l",   xlab = "w",   ylab = "k-attr",   main = "Near Pairs Attractive Force",   sub = "blue: UMAP, red: t-UMAP, green: PaCMAP wNB=1, yellow: PaCMAP wNB=3",   cex.sub = 0.75,   lwd = lwd,   col = "#4477AA" ) lines(uk$w, tk$attr, col = "#EE6677", lwd = lwd) lines(uk$w, pk$attr, col = "#228833", lwd = lwd) lines(uk$w, pk3$attr, col = "#CCBB44", lwd = lwd)  plot(   uk$w,   uk$rep,   type = "l",   xlab = "w",   ylab = "k-rep",   main = "Far Pairs Repulsive Force",   sub = "blue: UMAP, red: t-UMAP, green: PaCMAP",   cex.sub = 0.75,   lwd = lwd,   col = "#4477AA",   ylim = c(-2, 0) ) lines(uk$w, tk$rep, col = "#EE6677", lwd = lwd) lines(uk$w, pk$rep, col = "#228833", lwd = lwd)  pk2 <- pacmap_k(a = 2) pkm0 <- pacmap_k(a = 1000, b = 10000) pkm100 <- pacmap_k(a = 3, b = 10000) plot(   uk$w,   pk3$attr,   type = "l",   xlab = "w",   ylab = "k-attr",   main = "PaCMAP Attractive Force",   sub = paste(     "yellow: wNB = 3, grey: wNB = 2, green: wNB = 1,",     "cyan: wMN = 1000, purple: wMN = 3"   ),   cex.sub = 0.75,   lwd = lwd,   col = "#CCBB44" ) lines(uk$w, pk$attr, col = "#228833", lwd = lwd) lines(uk$w, pk2$attr, col = "#BBBBBB", lwd = lwd) lines(uk$w, pkm0$attr, col = "#66CCEE", lwd = lwd) lines(uk$w, pkm100$attr, col = "#AA3377", lwd = lwd)

text: Currently supported embedding methods, can used argument method parameter : "tsne" t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding   (van der Maaten Hinton, 2008). Barnes-Hut t-SNE (van der Maaten, 2014), selected   method = "tsne", bh = TRUE. "largevis" cost function LargeVis algorithm   (Tang et al, 2016). Input affinities calculated symmetrized using   perplexity calibration method t-SNE, normalized. "umap" cost function UMAP method (McInnes, 2017).   Unlike LargeVis t-SNE, UMAP uses un-normalized input weights,   calibrated via calculating smoothed k-nearest-neighbor distances,   rather perplexity (procedure similar, however). value   k controlled perplexity parameter. "tumap" Like UMAP, except output weight function   t-distribution one degree freedom, like t-SNE LargeVis.   simplifies gradient calculation compared UMAP, runs faster. "mmds" Metric Multidimensional Scaling (Borg Groenen,   2005), reduces "strain", .e. square loss input   output distances. "gmmds" Replaces input Euclidean distances   "mmds" geodesic distances calculated using k-nearest-neighbors,   style ISOMAP (Tenenbaum co-workers, 2000). value   k set perplexity parameter. "asne" original asymmetric Stochastic Neighbor Embedding   method Roweis Hinton (2002). "ssne" symmetric SNE method Cook co-workers (2007). "hssne" heavy-tailed symmetric SNE method Yang   co-workers (2009). "wtsne" weighted t-SNE Method Yang co-workers   (2014). importance matrix used degree centrality (column sums)   normalized input weight matrix. "ee" Elastic Embedding method Carreira-Perpinan (2010). "tee" t-distributed version Elastic Embedding (see   documentation https://jlmelville.github.io/smallvis/tee.html   description). "nerv" Neighbor Retrieval Visualizer method Venna   co-workers (2010). version differs presentation Venna   co-workers (2010), use precision values   determined perplexity calibration output kernel functon,   seems reflect presentation later publications, see e.g.   Yang co-workers (2014). really want version Venna   co-workers, use method "bnerv". "jse" Jensen-Shannon Embedding method Lee   co-workers (2013). "absne" alpha-beta SNE method Narayan co-workers   (2015). "chsne" chi-squared divergence version t-SNE   (Im co-workers, 2018). "hlsne" Hellinger distance divergence version t-SNE   (Im co-workers, 2018). "rklsne" reverse Kullback-Leibler divergence version   t-SNE (Im co-workers, 2018). "jssne" Jensen-Shannon divergence version t-SNE (Im   co-workers, 2018). "gsne", global SNE (g-SNE) method Zhou Sharpee   (2018). default, methods use dense input affinities gradients. t-SNE, bh = TRUE approximates repulsive interactions, neighbor input kernels can use approximate nearest-neighbor search.

To turn off visualization entirely: tsne_iris <- smallvis(iris, epoch_callback = FALSE, perplexity = 50, verbose = TRUE)  # Try the LargeVis cost function, using its default parameters: largevis_iris <- smallvis(iris, method = "largevis", epoch_callback = ecb,                           perplexity = 50, verbose = TRUE)  # Use a list with the method parameter for more control over LargeVis largevis_iris <- smallvis(iris, method = list("largevis", gamma = 1),                           epoch_callback = ecb, perplexity = 50, verbose = TRUE)  # Use the UMAP cost function and input weights (perplexity here refers to the # smoothed number of nearest neighbors) umap_iris <- smallvis(iris, method = "umap", eta = 0.1,                       epoch_callback = ecb, perplexity = 50, verbose = TRUE)  # Can also control extra UMAP parameters via a list umap_iris <- smallvis(iris, method = list("umap", lv_eps = 0.01), eta = 0.01,                       epoch_callback = ecb, perplexity = 50, verbose = TRUE)  # Make embedding deterministic by initializing with scaled PCA scores tsne_iris_spca <- smallvis(iris, epoch_callback = ecb, perplexity = 50, Y_init = "spca",                            exaggeration_factor = 4)  # Or use Laplacian Eigenmap for initialization (no exaggeration needed) tsne_iris_lap <- smallvis(iris, epoch_callback = ecb, perplexity = 50,                           Y_init = "laplacian")  # Return extra details about the embedding tsne_iris_extra <- smallvis(iris, epoch_callback = ecb, perplexity = 50,                             Y_init = "spca", ret_extra = TRUE)  # Return even more details (which can be slow to calculate or take up a lot of memory) tsne_iris_xextra <- smallvis(iris, epoch_callback = ecb, perplexity = 50,                              Y_init = "spca", ret_extra = c("P", "Q", "X", "DX", "DY"))  # Reduce initial dimensionality to 3 via PCA # (But you would normally do this with a much larger dataset) tsne_iris_pca <- smallvis(iris, epoch_callback = ecb, perplexity = 50,                           pca = TRUE, initial_dims = 3)  # Or use PCA whitening, so all columns of X have variance = 1 tsne_iris_whiten <- smallvis(iris, epoch_callback = ecb, perplexity = 50,                              pca = "whiten", initial_dims = 3)  # Classical momentum optimization instead of delta-bar-delta umap_iris_mom <- smallvis(iris, scale = FALSE, opt = list("mom", eta = 1e-2, mu = 0.8),                           method = "umap", Y_init = "spca")  # L-BFGS optimization via the mize package umap_iris_lbfgs <- smallvis(iris, scale = FALSE, opt = list("l-bfgs", c1 = 1e-4, c2 = 0.9),                             method = "umap", Y_init = "spca", max_iter = 300) # L-BFGS controlling maximum number of gradient evaluations and a further stopping # criterion for when the step size gets too small umap_iris_lbfgs <- smallvis(iris, scale = FALSE, opt = list("l-bfgs", max_gr = 1000,                             step_tol = 1e-6), method = "umap", Y_init = "spca",                             max_iter = 300) ## Example using distance matrix # Use gmmds: metric MDS using geodesic distances estimated from kNN distances # k is set via the perplexity argument. Use an epoch callback to get useful color # in the visualization iris_gmmds <- smallvis(dist(iris[, -5]),                        epoch_callback = function(Y) { plot(Y, col = iris$Species) },                        method = "gmmds", max_iter = 200, perplexity = 8, eta = 1e-4,                        Y_init = "spca") # The above should give equivalent results to the following version, # which uses the original data rather than a distance matrix. iris_gmmds <- smallvis(iris, method = "gmmds", max_iter = 400, perplexity = 8, eta = 1e-4,                        Y_init = "spca")  # Let smallvis choose an appropriate perplexity for you using the # Intrinsic Dimensionality Perplexity tsne_iris_idp <- smallvis(iris, epoch_callback = ecb, perplexity = "idp", Y_init = "spca",                            exaggeration_factor = 4)  # Use your own IDP candidate perplexities by supplying a vector tsne_iris_idp <- smallvis(iris, epoch_callback = ecb, perplexity = list("idp", 3:12),                           Y_init = "spca", exaggeration_factor = 4)  # Early Exaggeration tsne_early_ex <- smallvis(iris, exaggeration_factor = 4, stop_lying_iter = 100)  # Also late exaggeration to improve cluster separation tsne_late_ex <- smallvis(iris, exaggeration_factor = 4, stop_lying_iter = 100,                          late_exaggeration_factor = 1.5, start_late_lying_iter = 900)  # Barnes-Hut, approximate nearest neighbors, multi-threading settings # recommended for large datasets bhtsne_iris <- smallvis(iris, bh = TRUE, n_threads = 4, perplexity = 30,                         nn = "approximate", inp_kernel = "knn",                         exaggeration_factor = 12, stop_lying_iter = 250,                         Y_init = "spca") } # }
